newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour will not push for by-election yet.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour will not push for by-election yet.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party said on Monday it will not try to force a by-election in the vacant seat of Wirral South, where the ruling Conservatives had a majority of just over 8,000 at the last election, until three months after the November 3 death of the previous member, Barry Porter.
"There is a quite clear convention of the House that it is up to the party that holds the seat to call that writ," Labour chief whip Donald Dewar said on BBC radio.
"They have got to do that within three months of the death of a member. That three months is not yet up."

But replying to a question on whether Labour might itself move the writ, Dewar added: "I can assure you that if the Conservatives go beyond that three months, then that will be a very different situation."

If Labour wins a by-election in a safe seat at Barnsley East on Thursday, the Conservatives will be in a minority in Parliament. Dewar said it was Labour's view they should thus lose their majority on parliamentary committees examining legislation, making it much more difficult to pass bills.

But it was clear this was not the view of the Conservative MP Sir Fergus Montgomery, who chairs the committee which selects committees. "Clearly there is going to be an argument about that," Dewar said.
